hypothesis: x86_64 PGO was blocked by rustc's LLVM crashing while instrumenting the reth crate (SIGILL in libLLVM.so.23.1-rust-1.99.1 on stable). Nightly carries a different LLVM build, so the same two-pass PGO may simply compile. Worth one attempt because m8azn-3xl is the fastest box measured (4.51s) and PGO is worth -6% on ARM; nightly also brings evm2's tail-call dispatch, which was neutral on ARM, so a win here is attributable to PGO.
llm_commentary: PGO+THP on the fastest x86 box: m8azn-3xl 4.55s → 4.34s, -4.6% against the same-boot control. Real, but the smallest PGO gain of the four boxes measured (i7i -12.4%, i8g -10.6%, m9g -8.7%), and it does not take the lead: 4.34s still sits just behind m9g's 4.31s, at roughly 3x the cost per run ($0.0015 vs $0.00047). The ordering is the same pattern the whole project has shown — every lever that improves code layout or removes per-operation overhead pays least on the 5 GHz Zen 5 parts, which have the most headroom in raw clock and the least to recover from stalls. Practical read: PGO is worth taking everywhere (it is positive on 4/4 boxes, across both architectures and three vendors), but it does not change the hardware recommendation. m9g remains both the fastest and by far the cheapest per run.
